text: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE:March 30, 2026 ACLU of Idaho Statement on House Bill 822 Passing the Senate MEDIA CONTACT:Taylor Munson, tmunson@acluidaho.org BOISE – Today, the Senate voted to pass House Bill 822, a bill to create severe civil penalties for safety net adults in transgender minors’ lives. The ACLU of Idaho issued the following statement in response to the Senate’s decision: “The ACLU of Idaho is deeply disappointed that the Senate voted to advance HB 822, an extreme and unconstitutional bill that would severely curtail the ability of teachers, counselors, and medical professionals to provide support and medical and mental health care to minors when they need a trusted adult to help them work through questions about their gender identity. In some situations, the bill would force trusted adults to either ‘out’ minors to their parents within 72 hours, even when safety concerns call for waiting longer, or face devastating civil penalties of up to $100,000. “Idaho lawmakers have offered no credible evidence that a young person’s choice of name, pronouns, dress, or appearance poses any short or long-term harm to them; instead, HB 822 weaponizes the law to police youth expression and silence trusted adults, undermining free speech protections and violating the privacy of every Idaho student. “This bill would endanger LGBTQ+ youth, further isolate trans folks, and put all Idaho families at risk of government scrutiny over how their kids look or act. HB 822 is a sweeping act of government overreach that threatens our freedoms, dignity, and constitutional rights, and it has no place in a state that claims to value liberty.” ##### The ACLU of Idaho is a non-partisan, non-profit organization dedicated to the preservation and enhancement of civil liberties and civil rights. The ACLU of Idaho strives to advance civil liberties and civil rights through activities that include litigation, education, and lobbying.
